current.jp: 受付は一階にあります
current.kana: うけつけわいっかいにあります

structure_explanation.en: It's an existence/location sentence: the topic 受付 ('reception') is marked by は, and the verb あります (polite form of ある, 'to exist/be there') indicates where it is. に marks 一階 ('first floor') as the place of existence. In Japanese, saying where something is located uses this pattern 〜は 〜にあります.
structure_explanation.pt-BR: に marca 一階 ('térreo') como o local da existência

translation_literal.en: The reception is on the first floor.
translation_literal.pt-BR: Quanto à recepção, no térreo, existe/há.

translation.en: The reception desk is on the first floor.

gloss.en: to exist, to be, to be located

note.en: 連用形 stem (あり) of ある, before ます
note.pt-BR: raiz 連用形 (あり) de ある, antes de ます

objections.objection: Still reads "numeral (parte de '1º andar')", carrying the same Brazilian floor-numbering error into the token layer after the translation was changed to 'térreo'.
objections.auditor_hint: numeral (parte de 一階, o térreo)

structure_explanation.en: The sentence uses 私の番 (my turn), where the particle の links 私 (I) to 番 (turn) in a possessive relation. 番 is the subject marked by が, and the verb 来る (to come) is in the past 来た (came/arrived). Literally 'my turn came', which in natural English is 'it's my turn now'.
structure_explanation.pt-BR: A frase usa 私の番 (minha vez), onde a partícula の liga 私 (eu) a 番 (vez/turno) numa relação de posse. 番 é o sujeito marcado por が, e o verbo 来る (vir) está no passado 来た (veio/chegou). Literalmente 'a minha vez veio', que em pt-BR fica 'chegou a minha vez'.

translation_literal.en: As for my turn, it came.
translation_literal.pt-BR: Quanto à minha vez (私の番), ela chegou (来た).

note.en: past form (stem 来 of 来る + auxiliary た)
note.pt-BR: forma passada (radical 来 de 来る + auxiliar た)

note.en: auxiliary た that forms the past of 来る
note.pt-BR: auxiliar た que forma o passado de 来る

objections.objection: Both literal mirrors use the topic device ("As for my turn, it came." / "Quanto à minha vez (私の番), ela chegou (来た).") but 番 is marked by が, not は. Same rule-7 violation this batch fixes in four other records (8a5d2f4d0539, 8b4fe2088092, 8bc9ce5df658, 91d0f99f038f); shipping it here leaves が taught as a topic marker.
objections.auditor_hint: en: "My turn (が) came." / pt-BR: "A minha vez (私の番) chegou (来た)."

structure_explanation.en: 好き ('to like') in Japanese is a な-adjective (形状詞), not a verb. That is why the object of the liking is marked by が, not by を: literally 'chicken is pleasing (to me)'. です at the end gives a polite tone. In Portuguese we naturally translate it as 'I like chicken'.
structure_explanation.pt-BR: 好き ('gostar de') em japonês é um adjetivo-な (形状詞), não um verbo. Por isso o alvo do gosto é marcado por が, não por を: literalmente 'o frango é agradável (para mim)'. です no final dá tom educado. Em português traduzimos naturalmente como 'gosto de frango'.

translation_literal.en: As for chicken, I like it.
translation_literal.pt-BR: Quanto a frango, (ele) é agradável/do meu agrado.

note.en: polite form of the copula (です)

objections.objection: Rule violation shipping in 'after': 鶏肉が好きです has no は, yet lit_pt reads 'Quanto a frango, (ele) é agradável/do meu agrado.' and lit_en reads 'As for chicken, I like it.' — the topic device is applied to a が-marked noun. The record's own expl insists the point of the sentence is that が (not a topic, not を) marks the object of liking, so the literal mirror actively contradicts the explanation. Identical cases in this same batch (sent:gen-a793b5185326, sent:gen-a69cd9ea3fc0, sent:gen-a90b74a7cbaa) were fixed; this one was left.
objections.auditor_hint: lit_pt: "Frango (が), (é) agradável/do meu agrado." ; lit_en: "Chicken (が) is pleasing (to me)."

objections.objection: The English explanation ships with 'In Portuguese we naturally translate it as "I like chicken"' — an English sentence quoted as the Portuguese rendering. This is the exact defect the batch fixed in sent:gen-9ed462ea2cad (expl_en claiming what is natural in the other language); here it survives into 'after'.
objections.auditor_hint: In English we naturally translate it as 'I like chicken'.

current.kana: くるまをちゅうしゃじょうにとめた

structure_explanation.en: The structure follows the basic Japanese order: object + verb at the end. 車を marks the car as the direct object (を), 駐車場に indicates the place where the thing comes to rest (に of destination/endpoint), and 止めた is the verb 止める ('to stop/to park something') in the past. Note the use of に (and not で) because the focus is on the point where the car ends up parked.
structure_explanation.pt-BR: A estrutura segue a ordem básica do japonês: objeto + verbo no fim. 車を marca o carro como objeto direto (を), 駐車場に indica o lugar onde a coisa fica parada (に de destino/ponto final), e 止めた é o verbo 止める ('parar/estacionar algo') no passado. Note o uso de に (e não で) porque o foco é o ponto onde o carro acaba estacionado.

translation_literal.en: As for the car (を), in the parking lot (に), I parked (止めた).
translation_literal.pt-BR: Quanto ao carro (を), no estacionamento (に), parei/estacionei (止めた).

translation.en: I parked the car in the parking lot.

note.pt-BR: raiz conectiva de 止める (forma do passado com た)

note.en: connective stem of 止める (past form with た)
note.pt-BR: raiz conetiva de 止める (forma do passado com た)

note.en: auxiliary た that forms the past of 止める
note.pt-BR: auxiliar た que forma o passado de 止める

objections.objection: The fix landed on the WRONG token. The op targeted tokens[4].note.pt-BR ('conetiva' -> 'conectiva'), but in this record tokens[4] is 駐車場 (parking lot), whose note was null in 'before'. 'After' invents a note on 駐車場 reading 'raiz conectiva de 止める (forma do passado com た)' — a description of the verb stem 止め, which is tokens[6]. So (a) a factually false note is now attached to the noun 駐車場, (b) that new note has only a pt-BR key and no 'en', breaking locale parity with every other note in the corpus, and (c) the actual defect is untouched: tokens[6].note.pt-BR still reads 'raiz conetiva de 止める' (pt-PT spelling). Net effect: the patch introduces a new error and does not fix the reported one.
objections.auditor_hint: Restore tokens[4].note to null; apply the spelling fix at tokens[6].note.pt-BR: "raiz conectiva de 止める (forma do passado com た)" (leave tokens[6].note.en unchanged).

objections.objection: Same topic-device violation left in 'after': 車を駐車場に止めた has no は, but lit_pt says 'Quanto ao carro (を), ...' and lit_en 'As for the car (を), ...' — the は-mirror is applied to an を-marked direct object, and the parenthesis even names を. The structure_explanation correctly calls 車を the direct object, so the literal fields teach a structure the explanation denies.
objections.auditor_hint: lit_pt: "O carro (を), no estacionamento (に), estacionei (止めた)." ; lit_en: "The car (を), in the parking lot (に), I parked (止めた)."

current.jp: 日本語が大分上手になった
current.kana: にほんごがだいぶじょうずになった

structure_explanation.en: A change-of-state construction 〜になる ('to become'). 上手 is a な-adjective (形状詞); to use it with なる it takes に (上手になった = 'became skilled/improved'). が marks 日本語 as the subject that changed, and 大分 is the adverb 'considerably'. The past なった indicates the change has already occurred.
structure_explanation.pt-BR: Construção de mudança de estado 〜になる ('tornar-se'). 上手 é um な-adjetivo (形状詞); para usá-lo com なる ele recebe に (上手になった = 'ficou habilidoso/melhorou'). が marca 日本語 como o sujeito que mudou, e 大分 é o advérbio 'bastante'. O passado なった indica que a mudança já ocorreu.

translation_literal.pt-BR: Quanto ao japonês (が), bastante, habilidoso, tornou-se.

translation.en: My Japanese has improved a lot.

role.pt-BR: な-adjetivo que indica o novo estado

note.en: na-adjective (keijōshi); takes に before なる
note.pt-BR: な-adjetivo (形状詞); recebe に antes de なる

role.en: linking auxiliary for the change of state
role.pt-BR: auxiliar de ligação para a mudança de estado

note.en: に connects the na-adjective 上手 to the verb なる (上手になる)
note.pt-BR: に conecta o な-adjetivo 上手 ao verbo なる (上手になる)

note.en: past-form stem of なる; なっ + た = なった
note.pt-BR: raiz da forma passada de なる; なっ + た = なった

note.en: auxiliary た that forms the past of なる
note.pt-BR: auxiliar た que forma o passado de なる

objections.objection: The 'Quanto a X' device is reserved for the topic particle は, but lit_pt applies it to 日本語が: 'Quanto ao japonês (が), bastante, habilidoso, tornou-se.' — it even labels the particle as が while using the topic wording. The patch rewrote lit_en into a proper structural mirror ('Japanese (が subject), considerably, skilled, became.') precisely so the two would parallel each other, so after the change en and pt no longer describe the same structure and pt still teaches が as a topic marker.
objections.auditor_hint: O japonês (が sujeito), bastante, habilidoso, tornou-se.
